transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello. Well, I'm here because I've been having a lot of trouble dealing with this scar on my wrist. I mean, I know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me, but I just can't seem to ignore it. 

When I’m out at church, or sitting down to play bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It feels like it’s the very first thing they notice about me now, and it's really starting to bother me.
Do you find yourself doing things repeatedly because of the scar, such as trying to hide it, covering it up, or frequently checking it?

Yes, I do. Before I leave the house, I'll usually check my wrist in the hall mirror a few times. I try pulling down different sleeves, or I'll put on a bracelet to see if that covers it up better. And... well, sometimes I'll ask my husband if it looks obvious. He always says it’s barely there, but I just feel like I need to check anyway.
Aside from your scar, do you have any other persistent, repetitive thoughts or routines, like needing things arranged a certain way or repeatedly checking locks or switches?

No, I don't have anything like that. I mean, I'll make sure the front door is locked before bed, but just the once. I don't go back and check it over and over. And I don't have any rules about how things need to be arranged around the house or anything. It's really just this issue with my wrist that I get stuck on.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F42 (OCD) as repetitive behaviors and intrusive thoughts are exclusively limited to the appearance of the scar, and ruled out F40.10 (Social anxiety disorder) as social distress stems entirely from preoccupation with the perceived physical defect, confirming Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22).
